description: REQ-101's Edge Cases retain a scenario carried over from before the FIND-101 registry redesign: 'claude-p, or any other agent whose `is_self_funded` gate returns `false`, appears in the same telemetry-file directory listing (e.g. `$HOME/.anicca-founder/state/telemetry.json`, which `economy/ubi/run.sh` already reads for an unrelated purpose): THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it from this sum unconditionally' (behavioral-spec.md:150-154). Under REQ-105's now-finalized design, REQ-101's citizen list is read EXCLUSIVELY from `citizens.json` -- never by directory-scanning or otherwise iterating telemetry files independently (REQ-101's own EARS: the candidate list is 'READ from that registry, never hardcoded inline in this aggregation', behavioral-spec.md:135-136) -- and REQ-105's seed/append gate already guarantees claude-p is never a registry entry in the first place (behavioral-spec.md:388-391). This edge case therefore describes a code path (directory-listing iteration encountering claude-p's telemetry file) that cannot occur if REQ-101 is implemented as its own EARS clause specifies, making the edge case vestigial/confusing rather than load-bearing: a Phase 3 implementer reading it could reasonably (and wrongly) infer that REQ-101's aggregation is expected to also scan a telemetry directory, not just the registry, reopening exactly the kind of stray-enumeration path FIND-101 was meant to close.

REQ-105's own guarantee that claude-p is never seeded/appended into citizens.json, making the directory-listing scenario unreachable via the registry-only path
